Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  1-week history of painless swelling over left elbow; slightly warm, feels fluid-filled; minimal tenderness adjacent to swelling; full range of motion; no recalled trauma; desk-based job; physically active (runs 2–3 times/week). Known osteoarthritis previously diagnosed by GP.
- Relevant family medical history:  Denies family history of rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  No regular medications. New recommendation: ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (OTC). Allergies: peanuts; no known drug allergies.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Planned: inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP), infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and serum urate (gout screen). Results expected ~5–6 days after collection.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: New-onset, mostly painless, slightly warm, fluctuant swelling over the left olecranon region with minimal tenderness and preserved elbow ROM. No history of trauma. Skin over tip appears dry. Clinician does not think this represents septic arthritis.
- Impression: Most consistent with olecranon bursitis.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx and transcript):
  - Aseptic (nonseptic) olecranon bursitis due to pressure/microtrauma – High likelihood given painless/fluctuant swelling, slight warmth, normal ROM, absence of systemic features.
  - Gouty olecranon bursitis – Moderate likelihood; age/sex risk; variable pain possible; plan to check serum urate.
  - Septic olecranon bursitis – Low likelihood; lacks erythema, significant pain, or systemic symptoms; clinician low concern.
- Working diagnosis: Olecranon bursitis (likely aseptic).
- Management priorities: Symptomatic control with NSAID; evaluate for underlying inflammatory/crystal/rheumatologic causes; monitor for red flag features of infection.

Management Plan

- Medications: Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (OTC); stop if heartburn occurs.
- Tests: Send blood test forms to patient for ESR/CRP, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and serum urate.
- Follow-up: Arrange follow-up after blood tests (phone/video acceptable; in-person if symptoms worsen). Results expected ~5–6 days post-collection.
- Red flags/education: Seek urgent review if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/increases.
- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Aseptic olecranon bursitis (High): Painless or minimally tender, fluctuant swelling over olecranon; slight warmth; normal ROM; no systemic symptoms; clinician impression supports bursitis.
- Gouty olecranon bursitis (Moderate): Middle-aged male; acute onset with warmth and fluid; plan for serum urate testing.
- Septic olecranon bursitis (Low): Warmth present but lacks erythema, significant pain, or systemic signs; clinician not concerned for septic arthritis.

Quality checks
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse), height/weight/BMI/waist, urinalysis, immunization review, alcohol/tobacco/substance history, diet details, mental health screening, hearing/vision screening, oral/dental exam, ear exam, fasting BGL and lipids, STI screening as indicated, broader preventive health measures.
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Occasional unclear/inaudible segments and stutters, but clinical details sufficient for assessment.
